title: Raw interactive/structural HTML elements are refused in app modules
intent: A raw <button>/<input>/<select>/<textarea>/<table>/<dialog>/<form>/<meter> bypasses the app's sanctioned, token-styled primitive surface (accessible and theme-consistent by construction). The refused elements are declared in restricted-surface.json (restrictedElements); each has a sanctioned replacement in the stack's component surface, and the violation message names it.
reference: Button, Input, Select, Textarea, DataView, ConfirmDialog, Stack as="form" and Meter from @terpjs/react-core (BOUNDARY_SPEC.restrictedElements maps each element to its replacement).

runtime.rationale: The sanctioned components themselves render the raw elements into the built DOM -- every button on screen is legitimate output of Button. Compilation erases which JSX authored a node, and third-party components legitimately render the same primitives, so a DOM scan cannot soundly attribute a raw element to app authorship (unlike the layout contract's slot check, which verifies the identity of sanctioned components at one owned seam).
